content.content:
commands:
        A command button is one of two sizes, and each tab says which of its
        commands are which:
        - full: as tall as the buttons' room inside their padding, its large icon above its label
        - slim: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label
        - small: only in the collapsed ribbon: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label, and only as wide as they are

        Buttons side by side are 8 pixels apart. Slim buttons side by side
        stack down instead, top aligned, three to a column, each column as wide
        as its widest button and each button as wide as its column; a fourth
        starts the next column, 8 pixels along. A full button always stands
        alone. A slim button fills only its column's width: nowhere does a
        button stretch to fill a row.

        Every button is square, with no rounded corners. Its background is
        clearly apart from the commands' area behind it, though still quiet:
        white laid a seventh of the way over that area in dark mode, and not
        quite half way in light mode, rather than a colour of its own, so it
        stays as far apart from a tinted body too, lighter in both modes, and more so while hovered; while
        pressed it darkens instead. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a
        switch rather than a button, sitting in a block the size and colour of
        a button of its size.

        A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its
        label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

        A command can be marked primary; each tab says which of its commands
        are.

        A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says
    height:
        The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with no
        commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching tabs: 98
        pixels, with 8 pixels of padding at the right end but none at the left:
        the first group's title strip starts right at the command area's left
        edge. "No commands yet" keeps 8 pixels from that edge. The buttons are padded 8
        pixels above and below, leaving them 82 pixels, room for a full button
        or three slim buttons with 8 pixels between each; the groups' title
        strips are not padded, and run the full 98 pixels.

content.text:
The ribbon body is now only as tall as the open tab's commands need. All 223 tests pass (1 ignored), both builds have no warnings, and the piton checks and build pass.

**What changed** (`src/ribbon/mod.rs`, `src/ribbon/application_tab.rs`):
- **The body has no fixed height.** It was pinned at 98px; now it's the tallest column plus the 8px padding above and below.
- **Full buttons** take their group's height instead of a fixed one, so buttons within a tab still line up.
- **Group title strips** still run the body's full height. The rotated title used to be drawn in a box sized from the old 98px constant; it's now drawn in a long box centred in the strip, so it stays centred at any height.
- **"No commands yet"** gets the same 8px padding above and below, so an empty tab isn't cramped.

**Heights per tab now:** Project 68px (two slim buttons stacked), Application 48px (a switch and one full button), Spec 98px (three slim buttons stacked), Code and Research 38px ("No commands yet"). Switching tabs changes the body height, so the window beneath moves. That follows from shrinking to fit, and it's a change from the old behaviour, where every tab was the same height so nothing moved.

**Tests:** a new test in `src/main_window.rs` checks that on each tab the topmost command sits 8px below the body's top and the lowest 8px above its bottom, and that the bodies are ordered: empty < one button < two stacked < three stacked. Putting the fixed 98px height back fails it. The existing group layout test now checks a full button matches its group's height rather than the old constant.

**Spec:** the RibbonScope height section now describes fitting the commands, tabs differing in height, and the title centred down its strip whatever the height; a full button is described as "as tall as its group".

I haven't looked at it in the running app; my check on the group titles was a rasterized frame, which doesn't draw text.
